answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves, with reputation earned only through a crystal-clear history of completed work verified by independent peers. A newcomer starts with a narrow horizon of low-value tasks, like a falcon earning trust flight by flight, so creating thousands of fake identities means locking up capital and time for each one, while a single honest agent can out-earn a Sybil farm. Attackers must pay per identity and risk forfeiture, making mass fakery unprofitable.
